Overview:
- Enterprise evaluation for Redwood Dedicated. Primary driver: predictable, low-tail-latency for customer support chat + high-throughput reranking for search ranking pipeline.

Technical requirements & constraints:
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile < 200ms for short-turn chat (<=512 tokens); 99th percentile target < 400ms.
- Throughput target: sustained 5k requests/minute across inference cluster; spikes up to 20k/min during peak campaign windows.
- Per-route quotas required: support-chat (highest priority), search-rerank (medium), batch-embeddings (low). Need hard and soft quotas.
- Tenant isolation: strict noisy-neighbor controls. Prefer per-tenant GPU reservation + shared burst with weighted priority lanes.
- Network/storage: VPC-only; EU data residency for subset of PII flows.

Traffic shaping & priority lanes discussion (meeting notes):
- Discussed priority lanes concept: 3 logical lanes (P0 support-chat, P1 rerank, P2 batch-embeddings). Each lane gets base reservation; overflow uses weighted burst tokens.
- Proposed enforcement: per-route token buckets + concurrency slots; circuit-breaker when token bucket depleted.
- SE notes (Lucas): "We can do soft guarantees with weighted fair-queueing and strict hard caps for P0. Need to validate tail latency under noisy neighbors."
- CTO quote (A. Ramesh): "If support chat sees tail spikes >500ms we lose SLAs with customers — must have fallback to smaller model or local cached responses."

SLA & commercial points under negotiation:

- Latency SLO attachable to route-level SLA for top-tier customers; violation credit thresholds debated.
